title: pgm has no --help flag
cause: `pgm <command> --help` is parsed as an option that needs a value.
fix: Run `pgm help` (all commands with usage) or `pgm nodes <type>` (a node's inputs and options).

title: Detail further than `reach` from its surface
cause: A detail's guide (curve, points or courses rectangle) lies more than `reach` from the surface it decorates, often only at some control values, or where a joint crosses an opening.
fix: Put guides on or just off the face (1-3 cm in front of it), clip joint lines to the solid (do not run them across openings), or raise `reach` a little (e.g. reach=0.3). Check with `pgm sweep`: it tests every control end.
snippet:
G.guide('j', [x0, face_y - 0.03, z], [x1, face_y - 0.03, z])   # 3 cm in front of a face at y = face_y
G.stroke('wall-jointed', 'wall', 'j', profile='groove', width=0.012, depth=0.006, reach=0.3)

title: Extrusion profile crosses itself
cause: A 2D profile self-intersects, usually only at some control values (e.g. a notch wider than the wall at the smallest pitch, or two control extremes together).
fix: Keep every profile point monotonic in the direction you walk it; clamp derived sizes with mn/mx so notches stay inside the outline; test the corners (`pgm check doc --set pitch=2.4 --set height=5.4`), not only `pgm sweep`, which moves one control at a time. kitparts.fit_ring_depth sizes arch rings safely.

title: Python math on a kitlib expression
match: must be real number, not X
cause: C('...') and anything built from it is an expression (X), not a float: Python's math.*, **, abs() and comparisons cannot evaluate it.
fix: Use kitlib's expression functions: sin, cos, sqrt, atan2, pw(a, b) or sq(a), absx(a), mn, mx, floor, ceil, rnd, and lt/gt with iff(cond, a, b) for choices. Plain Python numbers are fine where no control is involved.
snippet:
from kitlib import C, sin, cos, sqrt, sq, pw, absx, mn, mx, iff, lt
r = sqrt(sq(C('pitch') * 0.5) + sq(rise))
w = iff(lt(C('depth'), 2), 0.4, 0.6)

title: Node type does not exist
cause: The node type is invented or misnamed (e.g. boolean, thickness, render).
fix: List real types with `pgm nodes`; read one with `pgm nodes <type>`. Booleans are `meshBoolean` or `boxBoolean`; rendering is the `pgm render` command, not a node.

title: Duplicate node id
cause: Two nodes share an id, often a helper called twice or in a loop with the same id.
fix: Give every call a unique id: include the side or index (f'impost-{side}', f'rib-{i}'); helpers should prefix their inner ids with the id they were given.

title: Module document not found
cause: The path or module name is misspelt, or the builder was not re-run after renaming the module.
fix: Run the builder, then `ls recipes/site/bench/`; the file is `<module>.json` with the module name you passed to kit.module.

title: Sweep failure: not a clean solid at some setting
cause: At one control end (or variant) a part becomes open, self-intersecting or degenerate.
fix: Read the `set` in the sweep failure and run `pgm check doc --set <name>=<value>` to see which part fails; clamp the sizes that collapse (mx(min_size, ...)) at that end.

title: Profile point count out of range
cause: A profile list is too short or too long for its node (the error gives the allowed range).
fix: Generate fewer points (lower the segment count of arcs) or split the part; check that loops that build the profile actually run.

title: @index (INDEX) used where it is not available
cause: INDEX (@index) only exists in options evaluated per instance (array/instance/ring rotation, scale, translation), not inside a shape's own options such as a revolve profile.
fix: Build one shape without INDEX and place copies with G.array / G.ring / an `instance` node whose rotation or translation uses INDEX.

title: Profile solid has too many corners
cause: A profileSolid outline has more corners than the node allows.
fix: Lower the segment count of curved parts of the outline, or build the part from simpler pieces.

title: Ports silently missing
cause: kit.module takes ports as a dict {name: port(...)}; a list of ports is accepted without an error but produces a module with no ports.
fix: Pass a dict and check with `pgm inspect doc`: its `ports` list must name every port.

title: Hollow turned parts (pipes, bored flanges)
cause: A lathe profile that stays off the axis without closing on itself leaves an open sleeve.
fix: Use G.annulus(id, ring_section) or G.pipe(id, axis, start, end, outer, bore): a closed ring section turns into a watertight solid, so pipe ends can show their bore.

title: Parts float apart (audit)
cause: A piece does not touch the rest within 3 mm (a tie rod ending in an opening, a plate hovering off a wall).
fix: Run `pgm audit doc`: its `detached` list gives each loose piece's bounds. Extend the piece into what carries it (a few mm of overlap is fine).

title: SDS shrinkage breaks 3 mm audit contacts or port fit
cause: Catmull-Clark subdivision without `limit=1` or sufficient creases pulls the smoothed surface inward from its control cage by more than 3 mm, opening gaps between parts.
fix: Always pass `limit=1, limit_normals=1` (and `creaseMethod='chaikin'`, `lodLevels=[2, 1, 0]`) on `G.subdivide`, or use `kitparts.cast_housing` / `kitparts.sds_cylinder`, and overlap mating parts by 3–5 mm.
snippet:
G.crease('body-cr', 'body-raw', sharpness=2.2, min_angle=30)
G.subdivide('body', 'body-cr', levels=2, creaseMethod='chaikin', limit=1, limit_normals=1, lodLevels=[2, 1, 0])

title: Pinched caps or high-valence poles on subdivided cylinders/extrusions
cause: Default N-gon caps on `cylinder`, `revolve`, `sweep`, `tube`, or `extrude` create high-valence poles and radial pinching when passed into `G.subdivide`.
fix: Pass `cap='quad'` on `cylinder`/`revolve`/`sweep`/`tube` (with even `sides`, e.g. 12) and `cap='inset'` on `extrude` before `G.subdivide`, or use `kitparts.sds_cylinder`. Inspect with `pgm check` (`sds`) and `--wire-cage`.
snippet:
G.n('drum-cage', 'cylinder', radius=0.15, depth=0.30, sides=12, rings=2, cap='quad')
G.crease('drum-cr', 'drum-cage', sharpness=2.6, min_angle=45)
G.subdivide('drum', 'drum-cr', levels=2, creaseMethod='chaikin', limit=1, limit_normals=1, lodLevels=[2, 1, 0])

title: Surface details vanish after subdivide or chamfer
cause: Mesh-rebuilding operations (`subdivide`, `chamfer`, `loopCut`, `shrinkwrap`, `weld`, booleans) drop upstream `0x8007` surface details.
fix: Always run `G.fasteners`, `G.rivets`, `G.seam`, `G.stroke`, `G.stamp`, and `G.text` AFTER `G.subdivide` / `G.chamfer` / `G.shrinkwrap` (and on FWN parts, after `G.smooth`).
snippet:
filleted_box(G, 'bed', [W, D, 0.06], at=[0, 0, 0.03], width=0.012, mode='fwn')
G.outline('bolts-g', at=[0, 0, 0.08], shape='rect', size=[W - 0.12, D - 0.12])
G.fasteners('bed-bolted', 'bed', 'bolts-g', head='hex', radius=0.014, washer=0.026, count=8)

title: Buried parts, transform typos on G.n, or unbored fasteners clipping shafts
cause: Passing `t=`/`r=` directly to `G.n(...)` (ignored instead of wrapping in `G.xf`) piles parts at the origin, and placing solid hex cylinders over studs or tight sheaves against cheeks causes solid interpenetration and jammed mechanisms.
fix: Always position primitives via `G.xf(id, src, t=..., r=...)`, use `kitparts.bored_nut` / `kitparts.bored_collar` / `G.pipe` around studs and shafts, and leave 3-6 mm radial/axial clearance on rotating sheaves, wheels, and drums.
snippet:
from kitparts import bored_nut, bored_collar
bored_collar(G, 'sleeve', outer_r=0.030, bore_r=0.016, length=0.04, at=[0, 0, 0.06])
bored_nut(G, 'nut', outer_r=0.034, bore_r=0.016, depth=0.024, at=[0, 0, 0.09])
